newsitem.title: POLAND: Foreign investment in Polish paper back to normal.
newsitem.headline: Foreign investment in Polish paper back to normal.

text.p: Foreign investment in Polish T-bills and government bonds returned to its average level this week after a brief retreat sparked by the slump of the Czech crown, a senior finance ministry official said on Wednesday.

"The level of foreign investment in Polish treasuries returned to its normal levels and just as there was no massive retreat as there was no overwhelming return," Piotr Dziewulski, head of the ministry's public debt department, told Reuters.

He said foreigners placed an estimated 170 million zlotys worth of bids at 1.6 billion zloty Monday's T-bill tender and bid for about 300 million zlotys at Wednesday's 800 million tender of two-year and five-year fixed bonds.
"The average level of Poland's treasuries held by foreign investors remains at about 10 percent," Dziewulski added.
